title: Rigveda 9.75: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.75: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.75 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 706v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.75.1-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 2, varga 33); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 706v
translation.original_text:
1a̱bhi pri̱yāṇi̍ pavate̱ cano̍hito̱ nāmā̍ni ya̱hvo adhi̱ yeṣu̱ vardha̍te | ā sūrya̍sya bṛha̱to bṛ̱hann adhi̱ ratha̱ṁ viṣva̍ñcam aruhad vicakṣa̱ṇaḥ ||
2ṛ̱tasya̍ ji̱hvā pa̍vate̱ madhu̍ pri̱yaṁ va̱ktā pati̍r dhi̱yo a̱syā adā̍bhyaḥ | dadhā̍ti pu̱traḥ pi̱tror a̍pī̱cya1̱̍ṁ nāma̍ tṛ̱tīya̱m adhi̍ roca̱ne di̱vaḥ ||
3ava̍ dyutā̱naḥ ka̱laśā̍m̐ acikrada̱n nṛbhi̍r yemā̱naḥ kośa̱ ā hi̍ra̱ṇyaye̍ | a̱bhīm ṛ̱tasya̍ do̱hanā̍ anūṣa̱tādhi̍ tripṛ̱ṣṭha u̱ṣaso̱ vi rā̍jati ||
4adri̍bhiḥ su̱to ma̱tibhi̱ś cano̍hitaḥ praro̱caya̱n roda̍sī mā̱tarā̱ śuci̍ḥ | romā̱ṇy avyā̍ sa̱mayā̱ vi dhā̍vati̱ madho̱r dhārā̱ pinva̍mānā di̱ve-di̍ve ||
5pari̍ soma̱ pra dha̍nvā sva̱staye̱ nṛbhi̍ḥ punā̱no a̱bhi vā̍sayā̱śira̍m | ye te̱ madā̍ āha̱naso̱ vihā̍yasa̱s tebhi̱r indra̍ṁ codaya̱ dāta̍ve ma̱gham ||
translation.text:
1GRACIOUSLY-MINDED he is flowing on his way to win dear names o'er which the Youthful One grows great. The Mighty and Far-seeing One hath mounted now the mighty Sûrya's car which moves to every side.
2The Speaker, unassailable Master of this hymn, the Tongue of sacrifice pours forth the pleasant meath. Within the lustrous region of the heavens the Son makes the third secret name of Mother and of Sire.
3Sending forth flashes he hath bellowed to the jars, led by the men into the golden reservoir. The milky streams of sacrifice have sung to him: he of the triple height shines brightly through the morns.
4Pressed by the stones, with hymns, and graciously inclined, illuminating both the Parents, Heaven and Earth, He flows in ordered season onward through the flee, a current of sweet juice still swelling day by day.
5Flow onward, Soma, flow to bring prosperity: cleansed by the men, invest thee with the milky draught. What gladdening drinks thou hast, foaming, exceeding strong, even with these incite Indra to give us wealth.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 706v (numbered 23v by the scribe) (OPenn image 707, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.75.1 ‹abhi priyāṇi pavate canaḥ-hitaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 707r (numbered 24r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.76.1 ‹dhartā divaḥ pavate kṛtvyaḥ›. Verses 9.75.1-5 end on this page.
